Title:  Accounts Payable Accountant

Vacancy:  2
Age:  At least 18 years

Salary:  Tk. 100000 - 170000 (Monthly)
Experience:  
Qualified or part-qualified accountant (ACCA / CA / CMA or equivalent), or qualified by strong relevant experience
Proven experience in a high-volume accounts payable environment, ideally across multiple entities and currencies (sterling and euro)
Demonstrable experience of supplier statement reconciliations and working within a controls-driven payment process
Proficiency with ERP/accounting systems (Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central experience an advantage) and strong Excel skills
Excellent written and spoken English, with clear and professional communication
Highly organised, deadline-driven and comfortable working to service-level targets
Reliable remote-working set-up with stable internet, and the ability to work UK/Ireland business hours
A proactive, problem-solving mindset and a commitment to confidentiality
Purpose of the Role
We are creating two new Accounts Payable Accountant roles to form a dedicated, remote AP processing team supporting the WH Scott Group finance function across the UK and Ireland. The team will own high-volume supplier invoice processing and a reconciliation-led payment control environment across multiple group companies.
These are hands-on, delivery-focused roles for capable accountants who take pride in accuracy, speed and control. The team will initially support W.H. Scott & Son (Engineers) Ltd (WH Scott UK), WH Scott Ireland and Re-Ropes, with Metlab and future acquisitions to be brought into scope as the group grows.
Key Responsibilities
Invoice Processing
Accurate, high-volume processing of supplier invoices across multiple group entities, ensuring correct coding, entity, currency, UK and Irish VAT treatment and approval routing
Match purchase orders, delivery notes and invoices to verify transactions, escalating mismatches promptly
Take ownership of the GRNI report and resolve outstanding items monthly, within the month-end timetable
Own the new supplier set-up process, including verification of supplier bank details in line with group controls
Supplier Statement Reconciliations & Payment Control
Complete monthly reconciliations of every supplier account to the supplier’s statement – 100% coverage, every month
Operate the group’s payment gate – a strict control applies: no supplier is paid unless their account has been fully reconciled to their latest statement. The AP team owns and enforces this rule
Prepare payment runs for approval, ensuring only fully reconciled supplier accounts are included, and document reconciliation status to support each run
Investigate and resolve reconciling items (missing invoices, credits, duplicates, pricing differences) promptly and to a clear audit trail
Complete AP-related balance sheet reconciliations within the set month-end timetable
Service & Responsiveness
Respond to supplier and internal queries quickly and professionally, working to agreed response-time targets
Work UK/Ireland business hours to remain fully responsive to the Group AP Lead, the wider finance team, operational sites and suppliers
Maintain organised, up-to-date records in the ERP system to support audits and reporting
Flag capacity issues early and support the scaling of the team as invoice volumes and entities grow

Position Summary
The Surveillance Officer plays an important role in systematic collection, verification, analysis, interpretation, reporting, and follow-up of health information and disease surveillance. This position involves implementing routine disease surveillance activities to identify, investigate, and monitor disease patterns, outbreaks, emerging health threats, and other public health risks. The Officer is responsible for ensuring timely, accurate, and complete surveillance reporting and sharing information with the Epidemiologist and relevant stakeholders to support early warning, preparedness, response, and disease prevention and control.
The Surveillance Officer will work closely with the Epidemiologist, Health Information Systems (HIS) team, MEAL Manager, Project Coordinator, health facility departments, Community Health Workers (CHWs), and relevant government, Health Sector, humanitarian, and partner stakeholders to strengthen surveillance systems, data quality, reporting, and timely public health action.
Key Responsibilities

Disease Surveillance, Outbreaks, Epidemiological Analysis & Data Management
Implement routine disease surveillance activities at assigned health facilities and ensure timely verification, reporting, and follow-up of surveillance information to identify trends, patterns, potential outbreaks, and priority public health concerns.
Monitor priority diseases, syndromes, unusual health events, emerging threats, and other reportable conditions through EWARS, DHIS2, HIS/HMIS, and other relevant reporting systems.
Provide verified surveillance data for programme, management, donor, and humanitarian reporting.
Maintain regular communication with relevant programme, technical, government, Health Sector, partner, and stakeholders regarding surveillance findings and emerging health threats.
Perform any other duties as assigned by the supervisor.
Research, Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting
Prepare surveillance summaries, which includes, however not limited to, situational analyses, epidemiological briefs, updates, tables, charts, graphs, and dashboards to support programme and management decision-making.
Assist in the preparation of technical briefs, bulletins, reports, research outputs, and publications.
Support data collection, analysis, documentation, and field-level implementation of epidemiological and public health research. (Active data collection might be required)
Conduct field investigations, rapid assessments, active case findings, and other epidemiological investigations when required.
Monitor surveillance implementation, data quality, reporting practices, and compliance with surveillance procedures and follow up on action points.
Maintain documentation of surveillance, outbreak investigation, response activities, findings, and follow-up actions.
Health Information Systems & Coordination
Conduct routine data quality checks and verify consistency between source documents, surveillance databases, health information systems, and submitted reports in coordination with HIS/ MEAL team.
Identify and follow up data gaps, inconsistencies, delays, and reporting issues with responsible departments.
Participate in relevant surveillance, health, epidemiology, outbreak, and coordination meetings and contribute surveillance findings as required.
Field Support, Capacity Building & Knowledge Management and Knowledge Translation
Provide orientation and technical support to health facility staff (technical/ non-technical) on surveillance tools, case definitions, reporting procedures, information requirements and data requirements.
Disseminate key surveillance findings, trends, alerts, and public health concerns to relevant health facility and programme teams.
Promote awareness of priority diseases, surveillance requirements, and timely reporting among relevant health facility and community-level staff.
Emergency Preparedness & Response
Maintain readiness to support disease surveillance and information management during outbreaks and other humanitarian emergencies.
Support rapid surveillance, data collection, analysis, reporting, and information management during disease outbreaks and other public health emergencies.
Provide timely surveillance information to support emergency decision-making, response planning, and risk communication.
Remain flexible and responsive to urgent surveillance and public health requirements during emergencies.
